methods.label: Hide as much white as possible
methods.explanation:
To prove the smallest possible white area, first find an amount that must show, then arrange the cubes to attain it.

A small cube can be completely hidden only if it is in the middle position in all three directions. Thus only the central cube has no outside face. Of the six white cubes, at least five must therefore show at least one face each. Each small face has area \(1\) square inch, so at least \(5\) square inches must be white.

This bound can be reached: put one white cube at the center of the large cube and the other five at the centers of five different outside faces. Each of these five cubes exposes exactly one face. Fill the remaining positions with the \(21\) red cubes.

The large cube has total surface area
\[
6\cdot3\cdot3=54\text{ square inches}.
\]
Therefore the smallest white fraction is \(\frac{5}{54}\), choice A.
